notes:
This appendix is almost purely qualitative: it contains no latency, throughput, GPU-hour, cost, percentage, ratio, or speedup claims at all. Consequently NONE of the arithmetic families in the audit brief (peak/mean, TPOT vs tok/s reciprocal, percentage deltas, share sums to 100%, GPU-hours = span x devices, denominator-definition checks) have any instance here -- there is literally nothing to recompute of that kind. The checkable relations reduce to (a) enumerated-item counts vs the lists that follow them, (b) version/date pins vs the git tag record and vs tab:ap-env, and (c) cross-reference resolution. I checked all of them exhaustively rather than by sample.

EXTRACTOR ADJUDICATION: the single defect flagged in extraction_notes.md (aiperf 0.11.0 cited to tab:ap-env, which has no aiperf row) is CONFIRMED -- I re-read apendice.tex:35-48 and counted 8 rows, none aiperf. The extractor's declined check (the two dynamo release dates and the monthly cadence) I DID run against the local mirror: both dates are EXACT, but the cadence claim is loose (40-day mean, not ~30) and the '-rc ahead of some minors' clause is factually wrong (the 0.x -rc tags precede patches 0.8.1/0.9.1, never a minor). Those are two findings the extractor did not have. Caveat the extractor was right to raise: this is a local checkout, so the tag set could in principle lag upstream -- but a lagging mirror cannot invent the v0.8.1-rc0/v0.9.1-rc0/rc1 pattern nor delete rc tags that once existed, so both new findings are robust to staleness in the only direction staleness can act.
